== Biography ==
'''Christian Glasgow''' was recorded in 1740 as a child of '''[[Glasgow-1504|James Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Murray-20395|Sarah or Sara Murray]]''' in a derivative chronology of the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian register.<ref name="Chronology">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html "Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context"], 1740 entry for Christian in the James Glasgow–Sara Murray household.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1504]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Christian’s 1740 occurrence is explicitly placed in James/Sarah Murray’s household by the derivative register chronology, agreeing with the preceding 1728–1732 children. Event type and sex uncertainty do not weaken the named father role.

Named child to the specific adult family role represented by the selected father; independent earlier ancestry is outside this assessment.

Next useful test: Inspect PRONI MIC/1B/6 Christian’s 1740 entry for full relationship and event wording.

Source basis already held: [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html "Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context" (https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html), 1740 entry for Christian in the James Glasgow–Sara Murray household.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


The derivative source does not quote the original entry, distinguish birth from baptism or state Christian's sex. The name Christian was historically used for women as well as men. The original register should therefore be inspected before gendered language or a later marriage is assigned.

No inspected record identifies Christian's spouse, children, death or later residence. The original register survives at PRONI under reference ''MIC/1B/6''; its marriage entries continue to 1769.

Christian is distinct from [[Glasgow-3492|Christian Glasgow of Glencorse]], who was born in 1708 to Robert Glasgow and Margaret Davidson.
